newsitem.title: CANADA: Falconbridge union sees full talks this week.
newsitem.headline: Falconbridge union sees full talks this week.

text.p: The union representing striking Falconbridge Ltd workers in Ontario said on Tuesday the two sides have made enough progress on shift scheduling to resume full-scale talks later this week.
Negotiations broke off on August 1 when about 1,400 unionized workers walked off the job at Falconbridge's Sudbury, Ontario operations.
But both sides have recently traded proposals on shift scheduling.

"We have an understanding of what the schedules look like. But the key to making the schedules work are the economic factors behind it," Rolly Gauthier, local 598 president of the Canadian Auto Workers union, said in a telephone interview on Tuesday.
Gauthier said he was hopeful full scale talks would resume by Thursday to discuss wages and other economic issues.
Falconbridge officials were unavailable for comment.
Falconbridge's Sudbury production last year, including custom feed, was 45,700 tonnes of nickel, 50,000 tonnes of copper and 1,600 tonnes of cobalt.
